brief: US bond yields hit a two-decade high last week, but the cross-asset vol reaction was mixed: rates vol (MOVE) jumped near a 1-year high while equity vol (VIX) held near a 1-year low. The note attributes the muted equity reaction to the yield move coming almost entirely from higher real yields (tighter financial conditions) rather than higher inflation expectations, leaving stocks near record highs. Credit vol widened more sharply (VIXIG, LQD both at multi-decade percentile highs) on spread widening, and oil vol rose despite falling oil prices, on geopolitical risk. Separately, single-stock dispersion (VIXEQSM) is rising ahead of Q3 earnings, and the note expects further dispersion given higher rates' historical link to it. Brazil's EWZ has the richest implied vol among global indices ahead of its Oct 4 presidential election, near a 4-year high, consistent with past election-driven vol spikes. Despite rising yields, demand for downside protection has fallen to a 1-year low: SPX skew is near 1-year lows and ~40% of top-100 stocks show inverted call skew, a bullish signal.
